Skytruth Analysis
Reported Spill Volume: 2 gallons
HARBOR STAFF NOTICED HYDRAULIC FLUID RUNNING OVER THE PORT-SIDE OF THE VESSEL INTO A SHEEN POOLING IN THE WATER. VESSEL WAS PORT SIDE TO THE DOCK AND HAS BEEN DOING ON BOARD REPAIRS FOR SEVERAL WEEKS SINCE THEIR ARRIVAL ON 11 JULY 2011. STAFF HAS PERIODICALLY NOTICES SMALL RELEASES OF HYDRAULIC OIL AND INSTRUCTED VESSEL CREW TO REPAIR THE PORT-SIDE CRANE. CRANE LEAK WAS REPAIRED BUT CREW CONTINUES TO WORK ON OTHER HYDRAULIC LEAKS. SAUSAGE BOOM WAS DEPLOYED AROUND THE VESSEL AND SORBENTS PLACED IN THE WATER TO SOAK UP OIL AT 1600 HOURS TODAY. SORBENTS WERE ALSO STUFFED INTO PORT-SIDE DECK TO TRAP ANY ADDITIONAL OIL ON DECK. WILL CONTINUE TO MONITOR SITUATION.

CALLER STATED A SCHOOL BUS WAS HIT IN THE FRONT BY A TRUCK THAT BACK INTO THE SCHOOL BUS. WAS THE INVESTIGATING OFFICER THE CALLER? YES WHAT PART OF THE BUS WAS HIT? THE BUMPER, GRILL AND THE RIGHT FRONT FENDER. HOW BAD WAS THE DAMAGE? MINOR DAMAGE BUT THE FRONT END WILL HAVE TO BE REPLACED. WAS THE VEHICLE(S) TOWED? NO. HOW MANY PASSENGERS WERE ON THE BUS? TWO. WHAT WERE THE AGE GROUPS OF THE PASSENGERS? PRE-K 5-6 YEARS OF AGE. WHAT WAS THE BUS NUMBER? 248. WHAT SCHOOL WAS THE BUS FROM? RAVENA CORYMANS SELKIRK CENTRAL SCHOOL. WHAT IS THE SCHOOL PHONE NUMBER(S)? 518-756-2282 (BUS GARAGE) WHAT WAS THE BUS’ DESTINATION? TAKING THE PASSENGERS HOME AS ONE OF THE PASSENGERS LIVED ON OLD STATE ROAD. THE SCHOOL BUS WAS TRAVELING SOUTHBOUND ON OLD STATE ROAD BEHIND A FEDEX DELIVERY TRUCK WHEN THE FEDEX TRUCK WENT PASS HIS DELIVERY STOP. THE FEDEX TRUCK BACKED UP WHEN THE SCHOOL BUS DRIVER THOUGHT THE TRUCK WAS GOING TO STOP AND TURNED INTO THE DRIVEWAY, BUT HE BACKED UP INTO THE BUS WHICH WAS ALREADY STOPPED.

SkyTruth Analysis
Lat/Long: 45.174722, -67.293889 (Explicit)
Report DescriptionCALLER REPORTS THAT A COFFERDAM THAT IS PART OF THE DECOMMISSIONING PROJECT OF THE MILL TOWN HYDROELECTRICITY GENERATOR WAS BREACHED SOME TIME BETWEEN DECEMBER 11TH 21:00 AND DECEMBER 12TH 4:00. THE BREACH RESULTED IN THE LOSS OF 10,000 TONS OF MATERIALS. THE MATERIALS CONSISTED OF 1,000 TONS OF RIPRAP R1000 (TYPE OF ROCK), 8,000 TONS OF 600ML MINUS ROCK, 1,000 TONS OF 3/4 MINUS (TYPE OF ROCK) AND A GEOTEXTILE MATERIAL THAT WAS PART OF THE DESIGN OF THE COFFERDAM. THE STATION IS IN THE MIDDLE OF THE SAINT CROIX RIVER AND THE MATERIALS FLOATED DOWNSTREAM INTO INTERNATIONAL WATERS. PRESENTLY, THE RIVER FLOW IS HIGH AND AS A RESULT, IT IS UNSAFE TO PERFORM MITIGATING WORK IN THE RIVER. EQUIPMENT HAS BEEN REMOVED FROM THE SHORELINE AND GRANITE BLOCKS HAVE BEEN POSITIONED TO PREVENT PEOPLE FROM APPROACHING THE SHORE. CURRENTLY, EVALUATIONS ARE UNDERWAY. CALLER STATES THAT THE CAUSE OF THE BREACH IS UNKNOWN AND IS UNDER INVESTIGATION. CALLER STATES THAT IT IS POSSIBLE THAT THE BREACH IS CONNECTED TO MATTER THAT THE DAM WAS BUILT ON. NOTIFICATION TO STAKEHOLDERS: ENVIRONMENTAL ENFORCEMENT DIRECTORATE (ECCC EED) DEPARTMENT OF FISHERIES AND OCEANS (DFO) CANADIAN WILDLIFE SERVICE (CWS) WILDLIFE ENFORCEMENT DIRECTORATE (ECCC WED) SHELLFISH WATER CLASSIFICATION PROGRAM (ECCC SWCP) NB PROVINCIAL MOBILE COMMUNICATIONS CENTRE (PMCC) USA NATIONAL RESPONSE CENTER (NRC)
